reviews.title: Worst company ever
reviews.text: After you take the time to sign up for the service they tell you that’s you need to pay. No courtesy to warn up front before spending time completing. Then even worse you start getting emails from them with no unsubscribe option. Apparently now I need to figure out how to disable the emails. reviews.title: Latest update is no good
reviews.text: Happy to fix review if the app is fixed. New problems: 1. Stops music when opening the app, 2. Record screen now requires an extra tap to get to a run, 3. Audio cues are broken.

reviews.title: Stay in Your Lane, Strava
reviews.text: Strava has become a Groupon DJ with a music-interruption fetish. Between the obnoxious Premium upsell pop-ups and the update that hijacks my music, this app is basically a digital paperweight.

reviews.title: Stop messing with my AirPods volume setting!
reviews.text: I’ve used the app for years and it does what I need it to do. However, I find it really annoying when it messes with the volume setting on my AirPods when I’m trying to listen to something. It hadn’t done it for a while, but now it’s back turning the volume down and I can’t turn it back up.  Problem goes away when I shut the app down.  I may have to switch to another tracking app.  So, beware before switching to Strava!

reviews.title: Incessant Pop-Up
reviews.text:
I don’t have a smart device like a watch and don’t plan on using one. Every time I open the app or go to the homepage a pop-up comes up telling me to connect a device.

I’ve already confirmed with the app that I don’t have a device. That’s an option. Why won’t this pop-up go away.

At this time, I will not be turning my free trial into a full subscription because I have to click “maybe later” every time I open the homepage.

Why is it so important to you that I connect a smart device? Please make this pop-up go away or I’ll never subscribe to this app and service.

I’ll probably stop using the app altogether in the coming days and go back to Map Runner unless this changes.

reviews.title: Relentless upselling pop-ups
reviews.text: I love this app, but it’s a shame with its success, they don’t realize yet that the constant upsell within the app is the most annoying feature across my entire phone. It’s a bad business model when you have to be annoying just to get to people to want to upgrade to your premium versions. It doesn’t work it just creates a bad customer experience. Would strongly encourage them to remove the pop-ups.

reviews.title: Poor, just poor
reviews.text:
The recent update to now start your activity are ridiculously large, there was no need for this, it’s ridiculou la and doesn’t improve usability, in my opinion.

In addition, and the most annoying and a reason why I’ll look at other fitness tracking apps, when listening to music (I use Spotify) and opening Strava, my music stops.  How anyone can think this is a good user experience is beyond me.

reviews.title: How to ruin an app in …
reviews.text: Congratulations on ruining your app! The latest updates prevent you from hearing the segments of your tracked run while listening to music. You might as well just discontinue it.

These decisions are not able to be challenged. Lesson - Strava doesn’t want you to give it a nudge from time to time OR take advantage of a tailwind.

reviews.title: Latest update rubbish on iPad.

Impossible to do anything, it keeps sending you from web site to the app, sending codes and codes and eventually when you get to the last klick - it doesn’t work!!! Hopeless!!! Why can’t I just delete my account simply??? Never going to download it again

reviews.title: Distance calculation wrong
reviews.text:
The app is great, except that it recalculate the distance by its own algo. Instead of taking the data from Garmin, which is main source of distance and applying it to the own map, Strava is taking the map route of our run, applying it to Strava map and recalculate the distance, giving significant mistakes in distance. I have run different places several times and I know the distance and pace, while Strava does use pace from Garmin source, but showing different distances. Developers better make it easier code, just show the map , but keep original data from watch. 
In overall app is cool.

reviews.title: New version breaks sounds on iPhone
reviews.text:
Have used the app happy for ages but latest version update 468.0.2 damps the volume on iPhone as soon as Strava recording starts sometimes to point of inaudibility.

Audio cues and Live Segments are off in strava settings.
1. Play audio (Overcast or Spotify) – volume normal
2. Open Strava – still normal
3. Start recording activity  in strava – other audio drops sharply (AirPods Pro 3, Bluetooth bone-conduction headphones, and the phone speaker)
4. Stop/save the activity – still quiet
5. Force-close Strava – volume returns to normal
Reinstalling Strava doesn't help. Started after the iOS 27 / Strava update. Other users report the same: reddit.com/r/ios/s/djG0WRkxtz

reviews.title: Impossible to cancel subscription

reviews.title: Auto charged $80 for USELESS features, refuse to refund

I got a 3 month subscription for free via adidas after which is auto charged my credit card for a 12 month subscription that they refuse to refund. The metrics and analysis are AWFUL. I already pay for a much better data analytics app, HealthFit.

reviews.title: Everything behind a paywall
reviews.text: I’ve been using Strava for a decade, and now I’ve noticed that everything useful and fun about the app is behind a pay wall, and that each week more and more features are added. At what point will anything on this app be free anymore?

reviews.title: Doesn’t sync with Apple Health
reviews.text:
Something’s gone wrong at Strava as the app worked a treat and was easy to use. 
Recently it feels clunky but my main gripe is that it’s stopped syncing with Apple Health. And, yes, I’ve done all the toggling of the buttons, closed it down, refreshed, updated and reinstalled. 
Eventually it pulls a run through until the next time when it’s back to square one. 
Maybe even worse as, despite everything, my last run isn’t showing.

reviews.title: Hidden cost

reviews.title: Highly Inaccurate

reviews.title: Used to be good

Unless you are prepared to pay the subscription, the free version of this app is VERY limited. I understand that there has to be a difference between the free version and the paid version but Strava has become ridiculous.
There are now other apps where either the free version is much better or the subscription is far cheaper. As others have mentioned, I find myself on Komoot.

reviews.title: Climbing Mode Garbage
reviews.text: There is a Rock Climbing mode that used to track time climbed and heart rate, which is somewhat useful information. Now it tracks time and horizontal miles, and tracks your horizontal movement around the gym on a map, which is useless and stupid information. Please change back to the way it was.

reviews.title: Comments on Other Activities Does NOT Turn Off

This needs to be addressed as my inbox is getting flooded so I have currently stopped commenting on other people's activities until this is resolved.

reviews.title: Sync with iOS workout / health not working

reviews.title: Doesn’t Track Accurately
reviews.text: I have logged over 1,500 miles in runs on this app. I have over 400 activites (runs) on this app. Needless to say, I was loyal for a long time. Maybe I didn’t care about my stats before, but now that i’m training for a race, I’ve become frustrated with the app for not accurately keeping track of my PR’s. And the support email is NO help. I have an activity on the app that states it’s my 5k PR at 17 minutes 41 seconds. On my Best Efforts page? The paced run I ran TODAY at 26 minutes. My best efforts puts my most recent run as my “best”, but it won’t acknowledge that I ran my actual best at 17:41. I’m trying to keep track of my splits for my race. If it just tosses any old run into my Best Efforts but wants to throw “your best 5k time yet!” in my face but not update the app correctly, I need to move onto a different platform. I’m proud to have ran a 5k under 18 minutes and the app can’t even properly track that. I’ve taken this issue to support countless times and the have an automated response that doesn’t help every single time. All that said, if you want accurate running results look for an app elsewhere.

reviews.title: No iPad app

And the browser experience for route planning and viewing heatmaps is terrible. I get that no one’s going to carry an iPad as their tracking or navigating device, but plenty will use one to plan activities and routes and analyse their performance. 

No when I try and import gpx via the website it normally fails. The quality of this app and service is really poor.

reviews.title: Consistently lose data
reviews.text: I run either holding my phone or with my phone in my pocket. My run data is consistently lost or corrupted by the run pausing itself, or it has several times told me I'm starting a hike route and I lose all my pace data, etc., while running. I've come to hate Strava, and I'm looking for a new app because I can't train properly with it, constantly losing my data and there being no way to fix it or correct it after the fact.

reviews.title: Tech issues poor customer service.
reviews.text: I’m a first time Marathon runner. I use Runna for the training plan and Strava for the data including being able to rewatch and study routes with times. The problem is Strava is unreliable and can shut off Runna does the same thing so I record in Apple Fitness which has been the most reliable. However when that information gets synced with Strava there can be missing maps on long runs. I’ve spent hours and literally weeks trying to deal with Strava customer service who have been of no help. Runs get duplicated in Strava and they all have different times. If you record in one it will be different than the others. I’m looking for consistency. Clear user friendly instructions and customer service that cares about customers. Right now the company is too big to see that the herd especially mainstream runners make up their customer base when another app comes along with better tech they will lose the customers. I’m waiting for that app. If you are training my suggestion is use Apple fitness get a plan and if you want to use Strava don’t integrate it with any other app even their own product Runna. It’s unbelievable no one on the tech side understands this.

reviews.title: App malfunction
reviews.text: I have used this app for years and used to love it. Suddenly it started calculating my heart rate zones incorrectly, based on my max heart rate (only 3 bpm between the start of Zone 5 and my max), which was throwing off all of my performance stats and suddenly my HR zone info, fitness and effort scores were useless. Of course I can manually adjust my HR zones but i expect the app to function properly since I’m paying so much for it each year. I have tried contacting Strava several times in the past 4 months. Initially it took them over 6 weeks to reply and each time they give a generic response. They are literally useless at helping me. Based on the lack of support and the app issues, I won’t be renewing my subscription this year.

reviews.title: GPS tracking is terrible

When looking on the maps it showed mine was all fuzzy and was adding extra distance in. So frustrating when I’m trying to train for a half marathon and I think I’ve been running less distance for such a long time.

It’s obnoxious and infuriating for a user who doesn’t want or need the premium. I am never going to pay for glorified Facebook - please, please stop asking me to.

reviews.title: Developed solely for watch wearers
reviews.text: Great app in principal. But they have neglected a pretty basic function. I don't want to wear a watch. I shouldn't have to wear a watch. But the developers have designed this app so it can only be used with a watch. Not only does it routinely secretly stop recording when you take a photo (iPhone using app to record), but the distances vary wildly. I've been on hikes with my partner where we both record, never go more than 10m from each other, and mine will say 17km and hers will say 15km. I know lots of people that don't use "smart" watches. Strava developers just straight up don't care if you're not into watches

reviews.title: Keep having issues
reviews.text: I really wanted to like this app, I kept hearing great things about it from other runners, but while I’ve only used it a handful of times, I’ve never not had an issue with it. At first I couldn’t get the audio cues to work, ok followed their guide and deleted and reinstalled app and it worked. Then I had issues with the auto pause, where it just decides I’m not running fast enough I guess? So it thinks I’m paused and I have to sprint for a sec to get it started again. Last run for some reason it just stopped counting kilometers, maybe it’s because I was somewhere rural and no internet but that’s mainly where I go. Tried this to replace Map My Ride, but may have to go back to it which I am very disappointed about because I really like the layout of Strava so much better, but if I can’t trust it to accurately monitor my stats I’m done.

reviews.title: Held hostage by their own login change
reviews.text: Strava removed Facebook login in March 2026 without ensuring users could recover accounts tied to old email addresses. I’ve been completely locked out for over 7 weeks, OTP codes going to an email I no longer have access to, and despite numerous support tickets I have received zero response. Not one reply. The app itself is fine but their support is non-existent and they’ve effectively deleted my account history through their own policy change with no recovery path. Avoid until they fix their support.

reviews.title: The opposite of product led growth
reviews.text:
Totally understand the need to monetise, especially if you’ve got PE pressuring for profit but rolling back features that have long been available to all users (not just premium), and require little to no compute / not user comparison is poor and not the way. Definitely not product led growth. 

I now cant scroll within my own segment history (just my ride data - no peer leaderboards). That’s my data I’ve trusted to Strava. I’ve been a staunch Strava user from the early days and a premium user for a long time but it’s getting harder to trust the platform now.

Nobody asked for this, yet you’ve foisted it on subscribers for no reason, literally making the app worse using money you didn’t need to spend.

reviews.title: Not simple.
reviews.text: The overall experience is overwhelming. The amount of clicks and choices and configurations necessary to just track workouts is overwhelming. Already on trial, and there are still options to pay for extra stuff. And you choose, and you configure and search. At the end of the day you have to manage an entire app to just have some extra info for your workouts. I’m looking for simplicity, and it’s one more thing to just spend 30min looking at the screen. I miss the old simplicity of apps. I have free subscription through my bank. I downloaded the app and started the trial before claiming the free year subscription I have. I just don’t want to have it for free. I have the option, but I’m declining. Please, add “simplicity” to the core of your business and users will thank you for that. I will be back to the simple workout app my watch offers.

reviews.title: Achievements Glitch

reviews.title: Beware of “hide my address” when signing up
reviews.text: When I first signed up for strava I used the hide my address feature from Apple. Everything was great until I ended up getting logged out from my account. Unknowingly, when I went to sign back in with Apple, I somehow signed in without using the “hide my address” feature and it made a second strava account linked to my Apple account. The app offered a free trial that I had signed up for. I didn’t realize that there was 2 accounts until I noticed my past saved workouts were gone. After at least an hour of troubleshooting I finally got into  my original account! Now the issue is that I can’t log back into the second account to cancel the subscription. I put a support ticket in last week and I have yet to get a response. From what I’ve seen on Reddit, their support team is awful at responding so here I am writing this review hoping that someone will see this and actually help me so I don’t get charged for a subscription I can’t even use.

reviews.title: Paywalled and Unstable

The friends and family plan is okay value if you have enough people to contribute. However my biggest gripe is that for an already mediocre product it goes down literally 3-4 times a month for multiple hours, sometimes upwards of half a day or more.

reviews.title: They Treat E-bike Riders Like Trash
reviews.text:
It seems like every update there’s some feature ensuring e-bike rides don’t clutter up the app for regular riders. 

Meanwhile we’ve been waiting 3 years for BLE cadence and power meter support. Features that would actually aid e-bike riders in getting more accurate metrics. 

I’m sorry to regular cyclists but e-bikes aren’t going anywhere and we are paying customers just like you.

After 24 hours I still can’t get a response. The AI bot keeps asking for the same information keeps telling me someone’s coming, but nothing happens. The after sales service is so poor. Help a paying customer should be a priority. All I ask is to get access to a subscription I’ve paid $99 for. How are you going to fix this Strava?

reviews.title: Horrendous

reviews.title: Bring back Average Soeed
reviews.text:
I used to love this app, then they decided to take away average speed which is EXTREMELY useful and replace it with a lagging speedometer. Useless because it is wrong, useless because it tells me what speed I was going 15 seconds ago and useless because it tells me nothing about my on going ride! If you are halfway serious with your biking, look for another app. It was a good run but time to find an app that gives people what they want, this is the biggest complaint and they persist in pushing useless features instead of what a person needs.

Now the latest version the speed updates every few minutes and shows what you speed was at some moment a couple of minutes ago. Elevation does not work. Always show zero even though I am not at zero. I have an idea, fire the current programmers and roll back to the version from about 2 years ago when this app worked. Just has a lot of features now that do not work. Don’t waste your money on this. They don’t fix anything.

reviews.title: Under-reports elevation gain
reviews.text: Way different vert/m climb to  barometric altimeter on watch. Slow sync of workouts from watch. Workout edit is clunky and can’t set defaults or which types of workout to auto-publish and which not to. A.I workout summary = vague feelgood woo. Subscription extras are just finer-sliced existing stats, nothing useful. Won’t renew premium.

reviews.title: Overrated and Faulty App
reviews.text:
This app gets a lot of attention as it tracks your progress, shows and gives you medals for your PR, and allows you to connect and share and get likes for accomplishments with other cyclist and runners.  I was suckered into paying for the full subscription by the hype this app gets with all the “if it isn’t logged on Strava it didn’t happen” acclaims.  Tonight I went on a near 4 hour ride and the app only tracked the duration and nothing else.  This app is overrated and glitchy to be useful.  

Map my ride is a much better app and you don’t need to pay extra to still get a great app experience.  Map my ride allows you to connect with other too but not as well as Strava.  However where it shines is if you want it to it gives you verbal updates in either variable time or distance increments with your current speed, distance, split pace, and average space.  Also what is cool is it will provide a starting timer so you don’t have to start the workout when you are stationary or just warming up.  

I actually did a quality test having both log a ride simultaneously and the stats were nearly the same however Strava gave me faster average speed so if you want to inflate your speed stats then Strava is for you.  

I now have to begrudgingly keep this app and make the best of it until my yearly subscription expires next January.  Don’t be a fool like me and give this app any of your money.   Keep it to humor your friends if you must.  Map my ride is so much better.

reviews.title: Useless in free mode
reviews.text: The free version of Strava used to give me some basic stats about a bike ride but now I literally just get the time? What a joke I can’t believe they’ve paywalled everything. This app is useless unless you pay them to use it.

reviews.title: Needs iPad app
reviews.text: Good app - map functionality is OK but can be improved (laggy, route creation is average). Needs dedicated iPad app as largely unusable outside of viewing activities given app dimensions take up c. 25% of screen.

reviews.title: Glitchy
reviews.text: “Something went wrong. Try again” and again, and again, and again. Very annoying considering I’m paying for the subscription. Not the first time this has happened.

reviews.title: I like Strava but feel a little they take advantage
reviews.text:
I use Strava once or twice a week for bike riding, and I do like it as a system. I can see most things that are useful to me on the free version. I paid for premium to test if it was worth it for me, it didn’t give me much more than what I needed so I decided to cancel it after 2 months. I am paid up until 27th of Feb, however, the one time I thought it would come in handy to plan a route on a trip away it restricts me from viewing routes etc unless I subscribe again!? 
I have paid for a month but they take features away before that month is up. It seems more like a punishment and it feels like I have been ripped off a little. 
I absolutely won’t renew my premium subscription because of this alone, I would look for alternative to this.

reviews.title: Goodbye Strava
reviews.text:
I first joined Strava over 10 years, back when it was the niche platform of choice for cycling/running/triathloning weirdos like myself. Why would I use any other social media when there was one dedicated to sport? It was amazing.

I understood why the subscription fees came in during COVID - it exploded in popularity, and had to cover the running costs incurred by the millions of new people signing up. However, recently, more and more features (many of which are very basic) have been creeping behind the paywall, and it’s now reaching a point where the free version is almost unusable. This is extremely sad, especially as many of these changes can no longer be justified, and it’s simply a way of forcing people to pay for their existing data.

So after more than a decade, I’m going to be waving goodbye to Strava. Thanks for all the good times down the years - hopefully you’ll recognise one day that this current money-grabbing approach is not the answer to long-term success.

reviews.title: “We sell your data back to you”
reviews.text: Classic tech bro bait and switch app. Want to see what you did? That’ll cost you.

reviews.title: Expensive, absolute soup of a UI/UX
reviews.text:
For free users (you’re already giving them your data), the UI/UX is an absolute mess. Lots of upsells to the subscription everywhere to the point where it’s confusing what you can actually do with a free account. 

Many features that are basically just aggregations of your data are locked behind paywalls - want to see the graph of your activities over a period longer than the last 12 weeks? You gotta pay for that.

I don’t want premium features, I don’t care about them, most of them come standard with Garmin so i don’t need them at all, but you can’t escape random buttons or full page upsells to the subscription
